analysis.title: Coffee Break: Shenzhen summit – the dawn of a multipolar world?
key_insights: The Trump-Xi-Putin meeting in Shenzhen, scheduled for 19 Nov on the sidelines of the APEC summit (18-19 Nov), is the first ever meeting of the three leaders. The agenda is largely unknown, though reports suggest nuclear disarmament and Ukraine will be discussed.

UniCredit sees the meeting as a milestone toward greater stability in a multipolar world and considers comparisons to the 1945 Yalta Conference unconvincing, since the current world is not bipolar and the three powers represent different civilisations.

Since New START expired in February 2026, the US and Russia have no legally binding limits on strategic nuclear arsenals for the first time since 1972. This raises the risk of a new arms race, while China and North Korea are expanding their arsenals.
President Trump has said nuclear arms control should be on the agenda. China has so far rejected this, citing its comparatively small stockpile.

UniCredit expects the meeting to be unlikely to resolve the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran, but likely to set the tone for how the three superpowers interact and provide a basis for an eventual settlement.

Nvidia's earnings and guidance came in above expectations and calmed nerves. Questions remain on AI investment returns, the sustainability of AI spending and the post-Huang leadership outlook. The initial market reaction may reflect relief rather than renewed conviction.
Anthropic's IPO prices later on 18 Nov. A valuation near USD 1.4tn with strong demand would signal that capital markets still back the AI theme despite scrutiny over returns and execution.
The US FOMC meeting minutes are released at 20:00 CET on 18 Nov. No UniCredit or consensus figures are given.
